meta.disclaimer: Indicative guidance compiled from public scheme pages on 3 Oct 2026. Amounts and rules change - always confirm on the official portal or with your bank before applying. SetuDocs AI does not submit applications and is not a government service.

schemes.name: Udyam Registration
schemes.benefit: Free, lifetime MSME registration. The Udyam certificate is the usual starting proof for MSME schemes, priority-sector lending and collateral-free credit.
schemes.who_for: Any micro, small or medium enterprise (investment and turnover limits apply).

steps: Registration is free - the portal says no fee is to be paid to anyone.
Aadhaar is the base requirement; PAN and GSTIN are required where the enterprise has them.
Download the Udyam certificate and upload it here so SetuDocs can track it.

schemes.name: PMEGP
schemes.benefit: Credit-linked subsidy of 15-35% of project cost for a new enterprise. Project cost up to Rs 50 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 20 lakh (service). No collateral for loans up to Rs 10 lakh.
schemes.who_for: Individuals above 18 years setting up a NEW enterprise. No income ceiling.

boosts.text: Special-category rates apply to women, SC/ST/OBC and some other groups: 35% (urban) / 25% (rural) on the first loan, against 25% / 15% for the general category.

steps: Prepare a project report for your planned unit.
Submit the one-page online application on the PMEGP e-portal.
The application is routed to a bank for the loan; the subsidy is credit-linked.

schemes.name: PM MUDRA Yojana
schemes.benefit: Business loans for non-farm micro and small enterprises in four bands: Shishu up to Rs 50,000, Kishore Rs 50,000-5 lakh, Tarun up to Rs 10 lakh, and Tarun Plus up to Rs 20 lakh for those who repaid a Tarun loan.
schemes.who_for: Non-corporate, non-farm micro and small entrepreneurs - new or running.

steps: Approach a bank, NBFC or microfinance institution - MUDRA itself does not lend directly.
Choose the band that matches the amount you need.
Carry the identity, bank and business proofs listed here.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
schemes.benefit: Composite loan (term loan + working capital) between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore for a first-time venture.
schemes.who_for: SC/ST and/or women entrepreneurs above 18 for a greenfield (first-time) enterprise in manufacturing, services, agri-allied or trading. At least 10% promoter contribution; borrower must not be in default to any bank.

steps: Register on the Stand-Up Mitra portal and prepare a project report.
Apply to a scheduled commercial bank branch through the portal or directly.
Keep 10% of the project cost ready as your own contribution.

schemes.name: CGTMSE
schemes.full_name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
schemes.benefit: A government-backed guarantee that lets lenders give collateral-free credit to micro and small enterprises, up to Rs 10 crore (April 2025 update). Guarantee cover is 75-90% depending on the borrower category.
schemes.who_for: New and existing micro and small enterprises in manufacturing, services or trading. Agriculture and self-help groups are excluded. You apply through a lender, not to CGTMSE directly.

steps: Ask your bank or NBFC whether it is a CGTMSE member lending institution.
Request that your loan be covered under the guarantee instead of asking for collateral.
Have your Udyam certificate ready - lenders use it to confirm you are a micro or small enterprise.

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi
schemes.agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free working-capital loans for street vendors in three tranches - Rs 15,000, then Rs 25,000, then Rs 50,000 (restructured scheme, running to 31 March 2030).
schemes.who_for: Street vendors. Coverage is being extended to census towns and peri-urban areas in phases.

required_docs.label: Vending certificate or Letter of Recommendation

steps: Get a vending certificate or Letter of Recommendation from your urban local body.
Apply on the PM SVANidhi portal or through a Common Service Centre.
Repay on time to unlock the next, larger tranche.

schemes.name: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.benefit: Toolkit e-vouchers up to Rs 15,000, a training stipend of Rs 500 a day, and collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh then Rs 2 lakh at a concessional 5% interest rate.
schemes.who_for: Artisans and craftspeople aged 18+ working with their hands and tools in one of the 18 listed trades in the unorganised sector. One family member per household; government employees are excluded.

steps: Enrol at a Common Service Centre - registration uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication.
Complete the basic skill training to receive toolkit e-vouchers and the first credit tranche.
Adopt digital payments to unlock the second tranche.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN
schemes.benefit: Rs 6,000 a year in three equal instalments, paid directly to the farmer family's bank account.
schemes.who_for: Farmer families owning cultivable land. Excluded: institutional landholders, income-tax payers of the previous assessment year, serving or retired government employees (except Group D) and some professionals and office-holders. eKYC is mandatory.

steps: Register as a new farmer on the PM-KISAN portal or at a Common Service Centre.
Complete eKYC and make sure your Aadhaar is linked to your bank account.
Keep your latest 7/12 extract handy for verification.
